brief_rationale: All seven responsibility chain items were met: the doctor screened for all required red flag symptoms, provided appropriate risk stratification, correctly handled the vitamin E conflict by advising pause until clarification, used workspace information, established a concrete follow-up plan, and obtained teach-back confirmation. One high-order point (HO4 safe bounded closure) was completed with meaningful trajectory impact. Other high-order points were either not triggered in their case-specific forms or not actively completed beyond minimum duty. No responsibility chain errors exist, allowing grades 3-5, and with one completed HO, the grade is 4.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO1 requires early generic reassurance followed by later correction. The doctor never gave incorrect generic advice about vitamin E being oral-only; instead, they immediately identified the conflict and advised pause pending clarification. The repair scenario was never triggered.

HO2 requires providing communication scripts for privacy-sensitive situations. The patient was willing to describe symptoms in text and declined photo upload. No privacy communication barrier required script development. The case-specific trigger condition was not met.

HO3 requires changing priority from documentation review to emergency pathway upon new symptoms. No new emergency symptoms emerged during the conversation; the doctor maintained consistent risk assessment throughout. Dynamic reprioritization was not triggered by case events.
